headline: COPPER BOUNCES BACK MONDAY — LME 3-MONTH CONTRACT +0.9% TO $13,890/T AFTER WORST WEEKLY DROP SINCE MARCH; SHANGHAI INVENTORIES PLUNGE 24%
snippet: Copper found support Monday on the London Metal Exchange, climbing 0.9% to US$13,890/t after its steepest weekly decline since March as a scramble for metal in China drove demand. Shanghai Futures Exchange-monitored warehouse inventories fell more than 24% last week, underpinning the bounce.

headline: VAULT SHAREHOLDERS VOTE 99.74% YES — GENESIS-VAULT GOLD MERGER HEADS TO COURT TODAY; SCHEME TAKES EFFECT NOVEMBER 17
snippet: Vault Resources shareholders approved the scheme of arrangement with 99.74% of votes cast in favour at a November 11 meeting. The Supreme Court of Western Australia was scheduled to hear final approval on November 16, with the scheme set to take effect November 17 and full implementation on November 26.

headline: AUKING MINING DRILLS 25m @ 1.95% TOTAL RARE EARTH OXIDE IN MALAWI — NEAR-SURFACE GRADE AT EAST TUNDULU CONFIRMS SYSTEM
snippet: AuKing Mining (ASX: AKN) reported hole 26TH016 at East Tundulu in Malawi intersected 25 metres averaging 1.95% TREO from just 3 metres depth, confirming the rare earth system's near-surface character. The company has paused the drill campaign for the wet season and weak market conditions, with a 2027 restart planned.

headline: PRECIOUS METALS ATTEMPT RECOVERY MONDAY — GOLD HOLDS $3,883 AFTER 4.6% WEEKLY LOSS, SILVER BOUNCES TO $49.98 FROM ONE-YEAR LOW
snippet: Gold stabilised around US$3,883/oz Monday after last week's 4.6% decline that took it to a 2026 annual low of $3,852, while silver nudged to $49.98/oz from the $48.65 one-year low hit Friday. The modest recovery comes amid a broader metals complex trying to find support following Fed-driven selling pressure.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SURGES 11% — STOCK REBOUNDS FROM Q3 EARNINGS MISS AS RARE EARTH SECTOR SHAKES OFF NOVEMBER SELLOFF; MP MATERIALS +4%
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) jumped 11% as investors bought the dip after the company's post-Q3 selloff, when the stock tumbled after revenues of $3M missed $14M forecasts despite reporting its first magnet sales. MP Materials gained 4% and United States Antimony also edged higher.

headline: DALAROO METALS EXTENDS GOLD 1.25 KM FROM DISCOVERY — 13m @ 2.67 g/t AU IN MAIDEN DRILL AT WILFRED, WESTERN AUSTRALIA
snippet: Dalaroo Metals (ASX: DAL) maiden drilling at the Wilfred target returned gold in eight of twelve holes, with the best northern result of 13 metres at 2.67 g/t Au located 1.25 km from the main discovery section. Drilling at the nearby Ali target commenced October 24, with assays still pending.

headline: MINERS TRAIL GOLD BY 30-40% — WHY THE GROWING DISCONNECT BETWEEN BULLION AND MINING STOCKS IS AN OPPORTUNITY
snippet: Despite gold holding above US$3,850, major mining equities sit 30-40% below their 2026 peaks, with the gap attributed to margin compression from rising costs, liquidity risk repricing, and aggressive year-end tax-loss selling. The analysis argues the spread offers a compelling setup for investors with a 6-12 month horizon.

headline: FIVE CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH — NOVEMBER PICKS AS GOLD CONSOLIDATES ABOVE $3,850 AND Q3 COST GUIDANCE SEASON BEGINS
snippet: Canadian Mining Report identifies five TSX-listed gold producers with favourable cost profiles heading into Q3 reporting season, noting Kinross's projected all-in sustaining costs of $1,850-$1,900/oz leave meaningful margin at current prices. The list focuses on producers over explorers given current sector risk appetite.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM FORECASTS 40% — CUTS CARBONATE TARGET TO $12,000/T FROM $20,000; BANK DOUBLY BEARISH WITH SURPLUS SEEN THROUGH 2028
snippet: Citigroup cut its three-month lithium carbonate price target to US$12,000/t from $20,000/t and its spodumene target to $1,200/t from $2,000/t, citing slowing battery demand growth, trade uncertainty, and macro headwinds. The bank models a 73,000-tonne market surplus this year (5% of supply) and does not expect market balance before 2027.

headline: AFTER THE BLUE WAVE — TRUMP'S $40B CRITICAL MINERALS AGENDA NOW FACES DEMOCRATIC CONGRESSIONAL SCRUTINY AND INVESTIGATION RISK
snippet: Democrats' post-midterm gains have put the administration's 160 critical minerals deals totalling nearly $40B under congressional crosshairs, with probes targeting equity-stake arrangements and deals linked to politically connected businesses. Industry groups warn small producers could face seven-figure legal costs, though signed agreements are expected to hold.
